test_title: PYST 22: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - English (Held On: 19th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:

Hoist with one’s own petard
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Defeated by one’s own plan**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Hoist with one’s own petard"** means to be caught in one’s own trap or defeated by one’s own plans. It originates from Shakespeare’s play "Hamlet," where "petard" refers to an explosive device. (अपने ही योजना से हार जाना) • **Example:** The hacker tried to infiltrate the system, but was hoist with his own petard when his malware crashed his own computer. • **Defeated by one’s own plan** refers specifically to situations where someone’s own actions or strategies backfire against them. (अपने ही योजना से हारना) • **Example:** The politician’s smear campaign ended up damaging his own reputation; he was truly hoist with his own petard. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: Rewarded unexpectedly** (अप्रत्याशित रूप से पुरस्कृत): Receiving a reward or benefit that was not anticipated. • **Example:** She was rewarded unexpectedly when her boss gave her a bonus for her hard work. • **Option 3: Praised for intelligence** (बुद्धिमत्ता के लिए प्रशंसा): Being complimented for one’s cleverness or intellect. • **Example:** The young scientist was praised for her intelligence after her groundbreaking discovery. • **Option 4: Promoted unfairly** (अन्यायपूर्ण तरीके से पदोन्नत): Advancing someone to a higher position without merit or fairness. • **Example:** The employee felt resentful when his colleague was promoted unfairly despite lack of qualifications. 31:T952, The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **Dull**.
